description.narrative: To address Gaza’s flooding challenges, Oxfam is taking steps to mitigate risks and ease the suffering of vulnerable communities. The strategy focuses on strengthening the resilience of flood-prone areas through essential WASH services, aiming to prevent public health crises by improving access to clean water, sanitation, and hygiene. This approach aligns with the needs assessments from September 2024 and OCHA’s winter strategy, structured around the following core pillar: Strengthen flood preparedness byimplementing effective WASH mitigation strategies that reduce the impact of seasonal floods on Gaza’s communities and improving WASH services in medical and educational facilities to ensure community protection and well-being. Since the War on Gaza began, Oxfam and its partners (PEF, PARC, Aisha, Jozoor, and ESDC) have delivered WASH services to 146 IDP sites, benefiting 433,195 individuals. Last winter, Oxfam coordinated with ECHO and IOM to deliver bedding kits from the Oxford supply center to Al Arish, distributing nearly 4,000 mats, blankets, pillows, and mattresses to 4,410 people. These efforts have built trust with affected communities, enabling Oxfam to respond swiftly to immediate needs. Currently, Oxfam is focused on repairing damaged water andwastewater infrastructure, rehabilitating water reservoirs, and cleaning manholes across Gaza. Oxfam is also providing water trucking, latrine installation, solid waste collection, and hygiene kit distribution. A multisectoral assessment by Oxfam <(>&<)> partners in August 2024 across 25 IDP sites highlightedsevere health risks due to poor sanitation. Skin infections were reported in 88% of the sites, followed by hepatitis (80%), intestinal catarrh (72%), and diarrhea/cholera (68%). Additionally, 72% of sanitation facilities were non-functional, requiring urgent repairs, and 100% of sites reported widespread malnutrition among children. Oxfam and its partner identified 233 high risk flood-prone areas, including stormwater basins, sewage stations, and lagoonsin humanitarian zones. Oxfam’s WASH program focused on 37 camps (Formal and informal) in Dair Al Balah and Khan Yunis where 5 (FGDs) revealed concerns about inadequate hygiene materials, sanitation, and water services. Diseases like diarrhea, hepatitis, scabies, and smallpox were linked to these poor conditions, with participants warning that latrines and sewage system are vulnerable to rainwater and flooding. Participants further reported that if rainwater accumulates and fills the sewage pits, mixing with wastewater, it would likely spread diseases, attract insects, and produce foul odors, particularly affecting children <(>&<)> other vulnerable individuals. Women highlighted the added burden of protecting tents during flooding, while educational facilities in Abu Baraka El Sahel and Harb Abu Baraka camps, serving 415 children, were reported to lack basic water and sanitation services, leaving them at risk of flooding during winter.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
